title: Side Door
family: Side pickup with sideways feed above an intact bumper
summary: Approach coral from the left side, raise it above the bumper, then feed sideways into a low tray. The side receiver needs its own chassis recess.
advantage: Leaves the front free and offers coral sideways without turning it. Flat side plates and small guide wheels suit the team's tools.
risk: Side pickup changes the driving approach and consumes side space. The lift, retention, and swept clearance remain unresolved.
firstTest: Mock up the full side bumper and one tube. Test floor reach, lifting outside the band, then sideways feed at 240 mm; reject any bumper overlap.
inspiration: Independent side-access sketch; no team geometry copied. Flat aluminum plates, polycarbonate guards and simple shafts are provisional.
states: Pickup at left side; hold one tube above the band; offer sideways. Whole-robot occupancy blocks a second. Lift drive, stow and jam release remain open.

title: Grab and Lift
family: Short two-link arm carries a single coral in jaws
summary: Small jaws grab a centered tube, lift it over the full bumper, and place it into a raised receiver. Two short links replace a continuous feed path.
advantage: Keeps hold of one tube through the transfer and avoids a long intake deck. Router-cut links and printed jaw pads are plausible starting points.
risk: Capture width is small; arbitrary tube angles may miss. Joint control and level jaws add work, and the new receiver must accept coral at 387 mm.
firstTest: Use two 220 mm mock links and simple jaws. Try offset and angled tubes, then carry one over a full bumper while checking grip and wrist clearance.
inspiration: Independent pick-and-place sketch, not a team's arm replica. Flat links and turned pivots fit the shop; drive ratios and jaw materials are unselected.
states: Pickup only a centered crosswise tube; hold in closed jaws; offer to a raised dock. Whole-robot occupancy blocks a second. Wrist leveling and stow are unproven.

title: Wheel Deck
family: Short front pickup and two powered wheel banks turn coral
summary: Low front rollers lift coral over the bumper onto a small powered deck. Two wheel banks run at different speeds to turn it for a rearward handoff.
advantage: Turns coral without swinging the whole intake. A short plate deck and separate wheel banks keep the turning job apart from the front pickup.
risk: The two banks may lose grip as coral turns. Added drives and sensing need tests; the receiver changes to a centered tray that accepts lengthwise coral.
firstTest: On a short two-bank deck, film one tube turning from 70 to 35 to 0 degrees. Try slips and offsets; then test the front lift over a full bumper.
inspiration: Independent differential-drive deck sketch, not a team reproduction. Flat deck, compliant wheels and simple shafts; motor and reduction choices remain open.
states: Pickup one tube; hold and turn on the powered deck; offer lengthwise. Whole-robot occupancy blocks a second. Speeds, sensing, reverse clearing and stow are open.
